item.title: Barbara London, Art Talk — Thu Oct 22, 4:30 PM — Manetti Shrem Museum (Shrem)
item.description:
Barbara London — a curator and writer, who founded the video-media Exhibition and Collection Programs at The Museum of Modern Art — will give a talk as part of The California Studio: Manetti Shrem Artist Residencies in the Maria Manetti Shrem Art Studio Program at UC Davis. London will speak on Oct. 22. London is an internationally acclaimed curator, advocate for the arts, writer and consultant with a practice that revolves around media, installation, and sound art. Recent curatorial projects include the exhibitions “Seeing Sound” at Independent Curators International; “Perpetual Motion” at the Perez Museum, Miami; and “Dara Birnbaum” at the Prada Foundation, Milan. London’s book, “Video Art: The First Fifty Years,” is in its third printing. London founded the video exhibition and collection programs at The Museum of Modern Art, New York, where she worked from 1973 to 2013.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Why We Ride — Thu Oct 22, 5:30 PM — Peter J. Shields Library
item.description:
Author Peter Flax will discuss his 2024 book on bicycling culture, and how the library’s archives on bicycles informed his research. Flax will share insights from Live to Ride: Finding Joy and Meaning on a Bicycle, which explores the unifying dynamics that bring bicycle culture together. With lyrical essays, character profiles, historical analyses, and engaging photography, the book makes a case that everyone who rides—whether they commute or enjoy nature or race—has more in common than they might realize. One section highlights the significance of groundbreaking bike lanes that were constructed decades ago in Davis—and how Flax was aided by photography and documents from the UC Davis Library’s Archives and Special Collections. Like the book, Flax’s talk will provide an inspiring and enlightening look at the reasons that people fall in love with riding and make the experience more meaningful and safe for everyone.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Salon Night: Meet and Learn from Local Reporters — Thu Oct 22, 6:00 PM — Heartscapes 1738 Pomona Dr
item.description: Free, all-ages, salon style casual discussion and Q and A with journalists about the role and importance of local journalism in/near Davis. In the spirit of Sacramento’s California Groundbreakers, we’re bringing thoughtful, salon-style speakers, discussions, and nights of fun and games to Davis! We’ll kick this off with an evening at Heartscapes Studio, 1738 Pomona Drive, from 6-8 pm. This event is free, all-ages, and open to the public, and we’ll provide snacks and drinks. Thursday, October 22nd will be a discussion on why local journalism – city and community papers, magazines, radio stations, TV programs, etc – is important, and what we lose in regions where our local news outlets close. We’ll bring in a few speakers for a casual conversation and Q and A on the roles local news outlets play in our communities, how many of us can benefit from them, why they’re at risk, and how we can all support them. item.title: Of Monsters and Men — Thu Oct 22, 6:00 PM — Sudwerk Brewing Co.
item.description:
Just in time for Halloween, please join the Davis Humanities Institute for a public conversation on horror and monstrosity through time and cultures, featuring talks by UC Davis Professors Michael Dylan Foster and Kathleen S Cruz. You’ll hear from foremost experts on Ancient Greek and Roman civilization and Japanese culture and folklore, and will have an opportunity to ask questions following their presentations. You can also enjoy themed cocktails (available for purchase) and participate in a short game of trivia to test your knowledge of all things horrific. item.description:

She wrote “Safe, Strong and Free,” Davis’ Take Back the Night March in 1984. item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Fri Oct 23, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Fri Oct 23, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Honkai: Star Rail × Currency Wars: Random Challenge! — Fri Oct 23, 6:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
Currency Wars – Random Challenge! Are you confident in your strategies and team-building skills in Honkai: Star Rail? Come and challenge yourself in the Currency Wars – Random Challenge! During the competition, participants will randomly draw special rules that restrict character selection, equipment, and battle strategies. Players must adjust their teams and overcome these unexpected challenges to achieve victory! The event also features Team Composition Rules and Fun Punishment Challenges, adding more excitement and surprises! After defeating each major boss, participants must complete a new fun challenge, such as singing, imitating characters, or performing funny actions. The player who completes the challenge in the shortest time while following all the rules wins! Are you ready to test your luck, creativity, and strategy? Join us and become the ultimate Currency Wars Master!

Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. item.title: Let's talk about Female Sexuality & Fluidity — Tue Nov 10, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community If you have ever questioned your sexuality, experienced unexpected attraction, fallen for someone who challenged how you understood your sexual identity, or simply wondered why we don’t talk more openly about women’s sexuality, this event is for you.
I thought I was heterosexual until I fell in love with a woman. Reading Sexual Fluidity by Lisa Diamond has helped me make sense of my experience, and it made me realize how many women might be navigating similar questions without having a safe space to talk about them.
Come join us in a frank, open conversation and connect with other women with similar experiences. item.description: This presentation brings together Catherine Hatzakos, Continuing Lecturer in the Writing Center, and Matthew Conner, Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences Librarian, to discuss tools, pedagogies, and learning outcomes for teaching about disinformation. Register here 2026-2027 marks the UC Davis Campus Community Book Project’s 25th anniversary, and our theme—civil liberties—leans into the Book Project’s legacy of promoting dialogue and engaging diverse perspectives and audiences. Our selection, On Tyranny: Twenty Lessons from the Twentieth Century by Timothy Snyder is a call to arms and a guide to resistance, with invaluable ideas for how we can preserve our freedoms in the uncertain years to come.
